title: CoreWeave Shares Close Lower Despite Goldman Sachs Upgrade to Buy

tickers.name: CoreWeave, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Investor concerns over the high cost of financing AI hardware outweighed the impact of a rating shift from Goldman Sachs on Oct. 19. CoreWeave shares finished the trading session in negative territory, reversing an early rally as the market focused on the company's credit risk. The firm's 2031 bonds are currently trading at a yield of around 15%, a level that analysts suggest reflects broader credit market volatility and anxiety over the cost of expanding AI infrastructure.

Goldman Sachs analyst Gabriela Borges upgraded the stock to Buy from Neutral with a revised price target of $106, down from $139, implying 73% upside from the Friday close of $61.39. The upgrade follows a 43% plunge in share price since Aug. 11 and a 24% drop over the last five sessions. Borges argues the market has overestimated CoreWeave's future cost of capital while underestimating returns, noting that new long-term contracts are starting at $13M per megawatt compared to a $10M per megawatt blended rate.

selectedTweets.text:
Goldman Sachs: "We upgrade CoreWeave from Neutral to Buy with 73% upside to our price target of $106 (down from $139 prior). The stock is down 43% since Aug 11 (2Q EPS) and 24% in the last 5 trading days, per our understanding due to a) ongoing volatility in the credit market, which raises questions on if and at what rate CoreWeave will
be able to finance their next phase of growth; b) debate on demand for intelligence at the frontier vs. off frontier, and whether changing mix impacts token monetization at CoreWeave’s customers, which in turn is key for the ecosystem to realize returns on compute investments. Going back to Finance 101, we see CoreWeave’s enterprise value as being directly correlated to the magnitude and durability of the spread between its unlevered IRR and WACC — and we think investors may be underestimating the magnitude of upward revisions to uIRR, and overestimating the magnitude of upward revisions to WACC."

"Based on our industry conversations, CoreWeave will still likely be able to raise DDTLs; and DDTL 5.0 and 5.5 both trade at or above their originally issued discount."

selectedTweets.text:
Goldman’s note this morning says $CRWV can still generate ~15% unlevered IRRs even assuming its GPUs are worth zero after five years with new long-term contracts starting ~$13M/MW versus ~$10M/MW blended today.

They also said the scary 15% unsecured bond yield also overstates the capital stack because Goldman puts CoreWeave’s blended cost of debt closer to 9% with most borrowing secured by GPUs and customer contracts while managed-inference and Omni can lift revenue per MW without requiring equivalent new infrastructure.

The catch is obviously efficiency because Goldman’s model implies a roughly 3-year payback versus closer to two years for $IREN and $NBIS.

With AI capacity still tight and CoreWeave already raising prices 25% in July, Goldman sees returns per megawatt as "biased to the upside" over next two years potentially growing faster than cost of financing its expansion.

selectedTweets.text:
Strong morning, weak afternoon.

Here's what's interesting: $CRWV finished lower despite Goldman Sachs upgrading it to Buy.

AI demand isn't the problem. The cost of financing AI infrastructure is.

CoreWeave's 2031 bond yield is around 15%.

There's a huge difference between selling GPUs and borrowing money to buy them.

That's why I prefer semiconductors, memory, optics, and testing over neoclouds.

The AI boom isn't necessarily ending. The market may finally be separating the winners from the risks.
